title: Morphisms out of the free DG module of rank one compute cohomology
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A differential graded algebra over $\mathbf Z$ means an associative unital graded ring $A=\bigoplus_{i\in\mathbf Z}A^i$ with additive differential $d:A^i\to A^{i+1}$ satisfying $d^2=0$ and $d(ab)=d(a)b+(-1)^ia\,d(b)$ for $a\in A^i$. A right differential graded $A$-module is a graded right module $M$ with $d^2=0$ and $d(ma)=d(m)a+(-1)^jm\,d(a)$ for $m\in M^j$. Write $D(A,d)$ for the homotopy category of these modules localized at the maps inducing isomorphisms on all cohomology groups; triangles are the distinguished mapping-cone triangles. Let $(B,d)$ be such a differential graded algebra and $M$ a right differential graded $B$-module. For $k\in\mathbf Z$ let $M[k]$ be the shift: $M[k]^r=M^{r+k}$, differential $(-1)^kd_M$, and the unchanged right $B$-action. For a cycle $x\in M^k$ (so $d_Mx=0$) the map $\mu_x:B\to M[k]$, $b\mapsto xb$, is a map of right differential graded $B$-modules. Sending $x$ to the class of $\mu_x$ in $\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(B,M[k])$ induces an isomorphism of abelian groups $$H^k(M)\xrightarrow{\ \sim\ }\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(B,M[k])$$ for every $k\in\mathbf Z$; in particular boundaries give the zero morphism. No boundedness, countability or commutativity assumption on $B$ or $M$ is made.

proof.text: Use the Hom-complex convention of [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived]. For any right DG $B$-module $N$, evaluation at $1$ gives an isomorphism of complexes $\underline{\operatorname{Hom}}_B(B,N)\cong N$. Indeed a degree-$r$ graded right-linear map is uniquely $f_x(b)=xb$ for $x=f(1)\in N^r$, with inverse evaluation. The Leibniz rule gives $d_B(1)=d_B(1)+d_B(1)$, hence $d_B(1)=0$, and $d(f_x)(b)=d_N(xb)-(-1)^rx\,d_Bb=d_N(x)b$. Thus evaluation commutes with the differentials. If $N$ is acyclic so is this Hom complex; therefore $B$ is homotopically projective by the cited definition.

source.place: Tag 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free; Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived (1), and its proof using Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective.

proof.text: For $N=M[k]$, the degree-zero cycles of the complex in Step 1 are precisely the maps $\mu_x$ with $x\in M^k$ and $d_Mx=0$: $d_{M[k]}(xb)=(-1)^k(d_Mx)b+x\,d_Bb$. The homotopy convention in [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived] identifies maps modulo boundaries of that Hom complex. If $x-x^{\prime}=d_My$, $y\in M^{k-1}$, the degree-$-1$ right-linear map $h(b)=(-1)^kyb$ satisfies $(d_{M[k]}h+h\,d_B)(b)=d_My\,b$, so $\mu_x-\mu_{x^{\prime}}=dh$. Conversely any such homotopy yields $x-x^{\prime}=(-1)^kd_M(h(1))$, a boundary. Hence $[x]\mapsto[\mu_x]$ gives an additive bijection $H^k(M)\to\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B,d)}(B,M[k])$. Addition is preserved since $\mu_{x+x^{\prime}}=\mu_x+\mu_{x^{\prime}}$; the sign $(-1)^k$ does not change the subgroup of boundaries.

source.place: Tag 09K1, lemma-hom-from-shift-free; Tag 09KY, lemma-hom-derived (1), and its proof using Tag 09KM, lemma-property-P-K-projective.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-dg-homotopically-projective-hom-derived] with algebra $B$, homotopically projective source $B$ from Step 1, and target $M[k]$. Its conclusion gives the bijection induced by localization $\operatorname{Hom}_{K(B,d)}(B,M[k])\to\operatorname{Hom}_{D(B,d)}(B,M[k])$. By [lem-sfb-dg-derived-admissible-triangles] the localization functor is exact, in particular additive, so this bijection is an additive map. Composing it with Step 2 is exactly the map prescribed in the statement, and proves the asserted isomorphism of abelian groups. The explicit homotopy in Step 2 proves the boundary clause. All degrees are arbitrary integers, and no argument restricts the size, boundedness or commutativity of $B$ or $M$.
